reason: The text explicitly demonstrates God's involvement in protecting and aiding the Hebrew/Israeli people. David invokes God's past protection, stating 'The Lord who delivered me from the lion and the bear will deliver me from this Philistine' (וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד יְהוָה אֲשֶׁר הִצִּלַנִי מִיַּד הָֽאֲרִי וּמִיַּד הַדֹּב ה֣וּא יַצִּילֵנִי מִיַּד הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הַזֶּה). The text culminates with the explicit declaration that 'there is a God for Israel' (יֵש אֱלֹהִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל) and that 'the battle belongs to the Lord' (לַֽיהוָה הַמִּלְחָמָה), showing God's active role in Israel's deliverance from enemies. David's victory, attributed to God's intervention, demonstrates that helping the Hebrew people overcome their adversaries is part of God's demonstrated purpose.
